title: Hacktoberfest has a place to start
summary:
Hacktoberfest app starters arrived, image models gained a metadata endpoint, and wildcard referrers made subdomain setup less repetitive.

A Hacktoberfest 2025 submission area added frontend app starters and two examples: CatGPT makes cat comics with image generation, while the Elevator Challenge asks players to persuade an uncooperative elevator. Contributors can optionally propose an app for feedback before building it. The React starter currently uses sample content, not Pollinations calls.

The image API gained an `/about` endpoint with each model’s name, tier, enhance flag, and maximum side length. Text model naming also took a round trip: short IDs remain the primary names, and longer model-specific IDs remain available as aliases.

Referrer authentication now accepts registered wildcard domains such as `*.example.com`, including nested subdomains but not the parent domain. Exact matches take precedence. A separate change added configurable concurrency caps for selected users of nanobanana and seedream; other users keep their tier-based caps.

daily.title: Hacktoberfest app starters
daily.text: Build a frontend-only Pollinations app from a single-file image-generation starter, or explore CatGPT’s cat-comic generator and an elevator-persuasion game for ideas. [Read the contributor guide](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

daily.title: Image model details
daily.text: The image API’s `/about` endpoint returns model names, tiers, enhance flags, and maximum side lengths as JSON. `/models` still returns names.

daily.title: Wildcard referrer domains
daily.text: A registered referrer pattern like `*.example.com` can authenticate requests from its subdomains, including nested ones. The parent domain still needs its own match.
